question: On 30 January, the Commission sent letters of formal notice to the Greek Government regarding its failure to transpose Directive (EU) 2022/542 and Directive (EU) 2020/285.

1 Directive (EU) 2022/5422 allows Member States, inter alia to: (a) set particularly reduced VAT rates (even lower than 5 %) and exemptions with the right to deduct VAT for essential foodstuffs, medical products, transport of passengers and goods, construction and provision of housing in the context of social policy, etc.

and (b) reduce VAT by 30 % in specific areas of their territory (for Greece, in the prefectures of Lesvos, Chios, Samos, the Dodecanese and the Cyclades, as well as on the islands of Thasos, the Northern Sporades, Samothrace and Skyros).

Directive (EU) 2020/2853 provides for simplified VAT rules for small businesses, as well as the possibility of exempting supplies of goods and services from VAT, provided that annual turnover does not exceed EUR 85 000.

Given that the Greek Government has not transposed the above directives (transposition deadline: 31 December 2024) and the two-month deadline for providing explanations has expired, the Commission is asked: 1.
Has the Greek Government responded, providing clear explanations for the delay in transposition?
If so, does the Commission consider the answers satisfactory and do they include a specific timetable for transposition?
What does the Commission intend to do to ensure that the above directives are transposed as soon as possible?
answer: EN P-002939/2025 on behalf of the European Commission (4.9.2025) The Commission attaches great importance to the timely and correct transposition of EU directives.

Due to the fact that Greece had not transposed by 31 December 2024 the provisions of: (i) Council Directive (EU) 2020/285 of 18 February 20201 and (ii) Council Directive (EU) 2022/542 of 5 April 20222, the Commission decided to open infringement procedures3 against Greece. The Commission sent its letters of formal notice on 31 January 2025.

As Greece did not reply to these letters of formal notice, the Commission decided on 17 July 2025 to send its reasoned opinions to Greece for failing to transpose the two directives.4 Greece now has two months to respond to the reasoned opinions and to take the necessary measures.
In the event of failure to do so, the Commission may decide to refer the cases to the Court of Justice of the European Union with a request to impose financial sanctions.
1 Council Directive (EU) 2020/285 of 18 February 2020 amending Directive 2006/112/EC on the common

system of value added tax as regards the special scheme for small enterprises. 2 Council Directive (EU) 2022/542 of 5 April 2022 amending Directives 2006/112/EC and 2020/285 as regards rates of value added tax. 3 https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/el/inf_25_273. 4 https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/inf_25_1628.
